title: Align platform circuit-breakers, idempotent endpoints, and SDK retry semantics to prevent retry amplification during tenant bursts
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Summary:
Customers have reported repeated request storms during tenant burst windows that resulted in cascading 5xx errors and escalations. Investigation shows a combination of aggressive SDK retry defaults (synchronous retries without jitter), insufficient server-side short-circuiting for overloaded tenants, and endpoints that lack idempotency hooks leading to amplified downstream load and non-deterministic failures.

Goal:
Design and implement a cohesive set of mitigations across the platform and SDKs to prevent retry amplification and provide safe graceful degradation for affected tenants. Deliverables: per-tenant circuit-breaker matrix, idempotent endpoint conventions for retryable operations, SDK retry policy harmonization (exponential backoff + jitter + idempotency-aware behavior), server-side short-circuiting (fast-fail and soft-503), telemetry/alerts, and a staged rollout plan with customer comms.

Scope of work:
- Define per-tenant thresholds and a three-state circuit-breaker (Closed / Throttled / Open) with configurable hysteresis and SLA tier mapping.
- Add idempotency-key header support for generation and validation on all mutate-like endpoints (uploads, cache invalidation, model start/stop) and ensure server idempotency checks are fast-path.
- Update SDKs (JS, Python, Go) to default to conservative retry semantics: max_retries=3, exponential backoff base=200ms, jitter=uniform, respect idempotency-key when present, and expose an escape hatch for customers.
- Implement server-side fast-fail path that detects overloaded tenant queues and returns structured 'soft-throttle' responses with Retry-After and suggested fallback model variants.
- Instrument new metrics: tenant_circuit_state, tenant_retry_rate, idempotency_key_collision_rate, per-route_5xx_after_retry. Add dashboards and paging alerts.
- Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate tenant burst patterns and verify no retry amplification occurs under expected traffic shapes.

Acceptance criteria:
- No increase in 5xx rate when simulating tenant burst in staging; retries do not produce amplified QPS to model serving.
- SDKs pass compatibility test suite and include new retry defaults in CHANGELOG.
- Customers on affected escalations receive staged rollout and opt-in link for early mitigation.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged server-side circuit-breaker in staging and internal dogfood tenant for two days.
2) Coordinate SDK patch releases (patch semver) to opt into new defaults but not force them.
3) Enable circuit-breaker for 5% of hosted tenants (low-risk) and monitor for 48 hours.
4) Expand to 30% then 100% with gradual tightening of thresholds based on metrics.
5) Document behavior in public API docs and send targeted comms to customers affected by recent escalations.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Too aggressive circuit-breakers may degrade user experience for bursty but healthy tenants; mitigate with SLA-tier mappings and conservative initial thresholds.
- Idempotency requires client participation; without keys, some ops remain non-idempotent — provide SDK helpers to auto-generate keys.
- Additional telemetry and checks add CPU overhead; measure and cap telemetry sampling.

- Design doc (working draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CIRCUIT-BREAKER-DOC
